This gorgeous 53 year old is 8 weeks out from her surgery and finally seeing the light of recovery ✨. She and her twin sister had twin surgeries with me, 6 weeks apart, and I can't wait to share their stories with you. They're both back to see me in February, but since all of our followup is virtual for now - we exchange texts, pictures and calls for monitoring progress and I've been keeping a close eye on her healing from afar. Swipe to see a diagram of what normal healing looks like time wise. As you plan your consultation and surgery dates, planning your recovery is so very important. She and her twin will both be featured soon in videos and such, talking about their healing so that you can get even more details from the patient herself 🤍 Other point about her: face shape In our late 40s, face shape often changes. In her pictures from age 40-45, she had a gorgeous heart shaped face, which with time became more square and boxy. As I envisioned her outcome, one of the most powerful maneuvers for her was to lift her cheeks, define her jawline, and alter her upper lip to reflect youth. She has always been stunning - that is a FACT. But I look at the pops of youth in her face now, and I'm just blown away by how her beauty is magnified this proportion and shape change. Clinical pictures and more video to come in Feb! Anatomical Deep Plane Repositioning to Rebuild Sculpted Structural Support] Hello everyone, I‘m Dr. Xiaohu, lead surgeon of the SANTA LUCIA medical aesthetics team. This comprehensive multi-angle case demonstrates the biomechanical power of deep anatomical repositioning in masculine contour reconstruction. The male facial framework is defined by robust skeletal landmarks; when retaining ligaments and the superficial musculoaponeurotic system (SMAS) experience gravitational descent, deep fat compartments shift into the lower cheek and submandibular zones, obscuring the natural jawline and softening facial folding. When managing structural descent at this depth, superficial cutaneous pulling cannot establish crisp skeletal margins and risks visible distortion. For this patient, we executed our primary Deep Plane Lift. Restore, Not Pull. Under direct surgical visualization, we meticulously released the tethering facial retaining ligaments and dissected beneath the muscular and fascial planes. Following posterosuperior vectors, the mobilized composite tissue was re-anchored at higher anatomical points in a zero-tension state, re-establishing stable 3D skeletal support from the base. Observing his post-operative views, the resolution of soft-tissue pooling exposes a clean, decisive mandibular angle and a defined cervicofacial transition, bringing back authentic masculine projection without artificial tension. This anatomical repositioning creates a reliable, durable structural foundation built to withstand time. DSvddx2kdft.text: facesbydrt Follow facesbydrt Edited • 47w ✨ Deep Plane Facelift at 47 - Kendall’s Journey 🔥 One of the most common questions I hear is, “Am I too early to have a facelift?” Kendall’s case is a great example of why age alone isn’t the deciding factor. This is her 3.5 month update. Kendall came in feeling that her lower face and neck looked heavier and more tired than she felt. She had tried fillers, but instead of lifting, they added bulk, especially through the lower face. When I evaluate patients, I focus on tissue quality, structure, and laxity. In Kendall’s case, the amount of laxity present meant that fillers, skin tightening devices, or RF treatments could not address her concerns in a lasting way and with noticeable but natural outcome. Here’s what she underwent: ✅ Deep Plane Facelift ✅ Deep Neck Lift ✅ Deep Neck Contouring ✅ Endoscopic Brow Lift ✅ Facial Fat Transfer ✅ Lobuloplasty 🧠 Some patients in their 30s and 40s benefit from surgery earlier than expected. The most common reasons are significant weight loss, inherited structural features, or genetic factors that are more than just about age.
